title: Paper-clay mushroom cluster sculpture
subtitle: A decorative woodland mushroom scene modelled from paper clay
excerpt: A cluster of five mushrooms in two species types, modelled and assembled from paper-clay air-dry clay. Freestanding on a shared base, the finished piece is about 15 cm wide and suitable as a table centrepiece or shelf ornament. Paper clay's strength allows the thin mushroom cap overhangs without cracking.

glossaryTerms.definition: Air-dry clay mixed with cellulose fibres for extra strength in thin sections
Clay thinned with water, used to join clay pieces

content.text: This cluster uses
paper clay

rather than plain air-dry because the cap overhangs and thin stalks need the extra strength the cellulose fibres provide. The five mushrooms are built as two types: three domed field-mushroom caps and two taller fly-agaric style caps with broader brims. No kiln is required.

materials.name: Clay slip (paper clay thinned with water)

content.text: Building the base and stalks
Roll a rough oval of clay about 15 cm by 10 cm and 15 mm thick for the shared base. Texture the top surface with crumpled foil to create a moss or soil effect.
Roll five stalks: three at 4 to 5 cm tall and 12 mm wide for the field mushrooms, and two at 7 cm tall and 10 mm wide for the taller fly-agaric type.
Score five positions on the base. Apply
slip
and press each stalk in place. Blend the base of each stalk outward into the base surface to strengthen the join.
Building the caps

For the three field-mushroom caps: form a smooth dome from a ball of clay and press the underside slightly concave with a thumb, forming a shallow bowl shape facing downward. The cap should be 5 to 7 cm wide and 3 cm tall.
For the two fly-agaric caps: make a broader, flatter dome 8 to 9 cm wide and 4 cm tall with a more pronounced rolled brim at the outer edge.
Score the top of each stalk and the underside centre of each cap. Apply slip and press each cap firmly onto its stalk. Allow the slip to grip for 2 minutes before moving on.
Drying and finishing
Dry slowly to
bone-dry

over three days under a loose cloth. Apply two coats of PVA. Paint: brown and cream for realistic field mushrooms, red with white spots for fly agaric, or tonal greens and creams for a quieter botanical look.
Variations
Add small polymer clay ladybirds or snails on the base between the stalks for extra detail.
Troubleshooter

items.problem: Caps tilt to one side as they dry
items.cause: The stalk was not fully centred under the cap and the overhanging weight pulled the cap to one side
items.fix: Support each cap with a small rolled pad of soft tissue or foil under the overhang while the join firms up. Check alignment before leaving to dry

items.problem: Stalks lean or fall over during drying
items.cause: The base join was not blended far enough into the base surface
items.fix: At leather-hard, apply slip around the base of each stalk and press a coil of soft clay around it. Smooth the coil outward and upward onto the stalk to form a strengthened root
